limitations: Counts describe a fresh uninterrupted 600-window run under the current code/config; resumed or failed work adds unknown discarded work and I/O.
Warmup is two lower windows per block. Empty replay skips each lower block's first window; upper-version changes flush replay. Event parity is global across nonempty events.

Each moving window includes one extra committed upper action at cutoff; upper-training windows also infer its value. That successor is created before the final SAC event and the world is then discarded by run.train.

The two measured scripted physical trajectories are not an empirical distribution of trained policies. Queue growth, graph size, history lengths, replay uniqueness and hardware variability can move runtime outside every shown range.

Profile operation times include their documented boundaries only. Moving evaluation uses full evaluation.replay900s in place of its standalone lower/upper inference and per-window JSON; physical/report construction remains separate. Standalone report/graph/GRU diagnostics are not added again.

No complete pure-lower hover replay was measured. The primary estimate retains hover component prices; a separate scenario charges it the full moving replay with extra upper work, without claiming a strict upper bound. The whole-replay versus fixed-section discrepancy is reported but not used to rescale training.
Checkpoint occupancy is enumerated exactly; 0/2 to 55 episode-record time/bytes are affine extrapolations. Pending PPO records use replay-record size as a proxy.

PPO fixture KL behavior does not determine future rollback frequency. Actor optimizer steps attempted range from 240 to 1440; accepted steps can be zero after rollback. Value steps remain 1440. Empirical fixture timing ranges are not theoretical bounds over arbitrary early-stop outcomes.

Unpriced residuals include scene/reset/startup cost outside measured collection, three scene integrity digests, initial module construction, report-history retention/GC, filesystem contention, checkpoint pruning, and future workload drift. No arbitrary reserve converts these unknowns into measured time.

Optional final-checkpoint paired stochastic testing is shown separately; secondary checkpoints, deterministic panels, baselines and five-seed multiplication are outside the one-seed training-plus-development scope.

metadata.label: baseline

sac_workload.sampling_note: Fixed stratified stress sample plus one prefix anchor per object; not an unbiased replay estimate.

initial_state_preparation.note: Optimizer slots are created by actual gradients. Parameters unused by these samples may still have lazy slots.

config.status: candidate discounted-control baseline; independent scenario windows; technical readiness does not authorize a research run

task.control_telemetry: synchronous causal full service reports; overhead uncharged, as explicit idealized assumption

objective.discount_status: Candidate baseline, not an optimum or performance acceptance: gamma_micro 0.99 per 0.5 s, gamma_macro = 0.99**10 per 5 s; half-life ~34.5 s. PPO uses discounted within-macro learning reward; evaluation uses undiscounted physical costs.

information.history_training: full_prefix_recomputation_and_full_BPTT_of_observed_arrivals; no cached old learned hidden states

randomness.stream_schedules: explicitly specified in section17; CPU Dirichlet uses fork_rng and persistent dedicated states

research.note: Technical configuration confirmations are not authorization to launch research training. Each 900 s window resets to an independent scenario and ends by truncation with a real successor from the pre-reset trajectory; no cross-window physical checkpoint is needed. Gamma/lambda are candidate baseline values, not claimed optimal or performance-accepted. Schedule and network numbers unchanged.

metadata.methodology: Restore exact weights/optimizer/counters/RNG before every repetition; setup is excluded. Wall-clock runs have no cProfile or record_function wrappers; CUDA synchronization only at operation boundaries. RSS peak is sampled at 10 ms, so narrow peaks can be missed. Graph preparation includes Python building and transfers; identify actual copies using aten::_to_copy/copy_ and CUDA memcpy events, not the entire preparation scope.
limitations: Four replay objects and five PPO objects reuse these trajectories.
Normal/backlog mean empirical queue-count percentile bands, not configured arrival regimes.
Fresh initial state has lazy Adam slots; timings include their first allocation unless an initialized state is supplied.
PPO is a synthetic update workload on scripted states, not an on-policy rollout.
Evaluation replay does not execute chosen actions and cannot measure closed-loop cost or physics time.
Checkpoint uses two actual replay episodes; no claim about a full 55-episode buffer.

raw.limitation: Single 60-second CPU script per mode; same external seeds and routing. This is not a 900-second measurement, and extrapolation can miss queue/history growth. Inclusive component timers must not be added.
